claims.text: On October 6th AEP Texas said it is using Pano AI cameras to detect smoke or ignition in its west Texas service territory.
claims.quote:
October 6, 2026
AEP Texas is using artificial intelligence and innovative technology to help protect customers and communities from the threat to wildfire.
claims.scope_note: AEP's own community page, dated October 6, 2026. The page names no county or town.

claims.text: As of early October, 16 cameras were installed, and AEP Texas plans 56 by February 2027.
claims.quote: As of early October, 16 Pano AI cameras have been installed across the service territory. By February 2027, AEP Texas plans to have a total of 56 cameras installed.
claims.scope_note: Company count and plan, no independent count.

claims.text: Each camera sits on an approximately 200-foot communications tower with a 360-degree view.
claims.quote: Each camera is installed on an approximately 200-foot-tall communications tower with a 360-degree view of the surrounding area.

claims.text: When one camera detects heat or smoke, the AEP Texas team is notified by email or text message.
claims.quote: When one camera detects heat or smoke, the team receives a notification via email or text message.
claims.scope_note: The page describes AEP's team as the first recipient and does not describe a 911 or fire department step.

claims.text: AI software sends notifications to AEP Texas within an estimated ten minutes of detection.
claims.quote: The cameras use a powerful camera and technology to detect heat, smoke or ignition and employ artificial intelligence software to send notifications to AEP Texas within an estimated ten minutes of detection.
claims.scope_note: The ten minutes is AEP's estimate, not a measured time.

claims.text: The cameras do not prevent wildfires. AEP says they give situational awareness it can share with first responders.
claims.quote: Although the cameras do not prevent wildfires from happening, Wildfire Mitigation and Response Lead Floyd Watkins said they provide situational awareness for AEP Texas that can be shared with external resources like first responders.
claims.scope_note: Sharing with responders is described as possible, not as a built-in alert.

claims.text: Since the official launch earlier this year, AEP Texas has had no major fire requiring its response.
claims.quote: Since the official launch earlier this year, Watkins said there has not been a major fire which has required an AEP Texas response
claims.scope_note: Self-report. No launch date and no response record are published.

claims.text: Floyd Watkins, AEP Texas Wildfire Mitigation and Response Lead, said the real value is reducing the time between a potential ignition and actionable awareness.
claims.quote: “The real value is not just detection — it is reducing the time between a potential ignition and actionable awareness.”
claims.scope_note: Direct quote from the named lead.

claims.text: AEP Texas filed its Wildfire Mitigation Plan with the Public Utility Commission of Texas on August 24th.
claims.quote: AEP Texas has filed a Wildfire Mitigation Plan (WMP) with the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT)
claims.scope_note: Trade press. The date comes from the sentence 'The plan, filed Aug. 24, builds on AEP Texas’ previously filed Resiliency Plan'. The summary does not name cameras, although AEP's own page says the cameras are part of its Resiliency and Wildfire Mitigation Plans.

claims.text: As reported in late September, only eight of the 161 utilities required to file wildfire plans had done so, according to the Public Utility Commission of Texas.
claims.quote: only eight of the 161 utility companies required to submit plans have done so, according to the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT).
claims.scope_note: Count as reported by local TV from PUCT figures given to lawmakers.

claims.text: Subject to Public Utility Commission approval, the plan is expected to take effect in January 2027.
claims.quote: Subject to PUCT approval, the plan is expected to take effect in January 2027.
claims.scope_note: Trade press. The date comes from the sentence 'The plan, filed Aug. 24, builds on AEP Texas’ previously filed Resiliency Plan'. The summary does not name cameras, although AEP's own page says the cameras are part of its Resiliency and Wildfire Mitigation Plans.
